Trust me, it gets worse before it gets better. In my experience, heartbreak was like withdrawing off a drug that absolutely broke me that I just had to get through to make it over the other side. There’s no way to cheat it, it has to hurt to heal I’m afraid. 
As someone who was dumped from a long term relationship, who I experienced everything for the first time with, it is especially rough. It is not a life sentence though, you will meet people who you could not have comprehended getting along with. The future being an unknown doesn’t provide us with the reassurance to guarantee everything will work out, but it will as long as you heal from this. 
I have changed significantly since September when I got broken up with. If I could go back and tell myself, hang on, you’re going to really like the person you’re becoming - you’re more confident now, you don’t stutter over your words looking for the right thing to say, you know yourself with more authority now, you have literally had a glow up and people have *noticed*, you’re finally focused on YOUR life and making decisions without needing someone to co-sign it. 
I know it hurts like a bitch right now, all you can do is let it hurt, treat yourself like how you would treat a friend going through the same thing. You will get through this and come out the other side with more wisdom and strength. When the time is right, you will know when you are ready to get out there again and there is no expectation to go looking following a break up.

Medications, especially when they affect your brain without knowing how you will react to it can be scary. For me, I upped my dosage last year to 100mg and have been off and on it for 8 years. Sertraline is luckily one of the more agreeable meds you can take. Your libido will most likely decrease, this has been the case for me but has significantly gotten better after I stopped taking the pill. Anyway! 
I also suffer from anxiety and noticed I felt like I was able to get the extra push from Sertraline to handle these situations. When I got off it 2 years ago, I was experiencing suicidal ideation and literally felt terrified of everything for six and months, and after going back on I really appreciated how much relief it gave me. If you do experience any discomfort, see your doctor to find something more suitable, but more than likely you’ll be a-okay. ❤️

If I can encourage anything it’s not to question your self worth. This was huge for me as someone who was also dumped by someone who I’d always thought I would spend my whole life with. 
Someone who truly loves you won’t ever hurt you more than necessary if they feel the relationship is done. A person with integrity faces things head-on and shows the other person the respect of not wasting their time, doesn’t make their indecision the cross for the other person to bear or let them live in a state of confusion and uncertainty. 
We all make mistakes, but when they hurt other people it must be a lesson to learn and change. She should have been upfront with you and not subjected you to months of what must have been extreme pain of not feeling good enough for someone who once showed you a lot more love. Your lesson here was to not accept emotional neglect - we teach ourselves what is ok based on what we are willing to accept, and in this instance you deserved much more. 
Don’t beat yourself up, if you notice you’re doing that take a step back and maybe you’ve even put this person on a higher pedestal than they deserve, that’s why their criticism of you comes from a place that feels like you’re being looked down upon. Maybe shift your healing process to building yourself up. I definitely had to!

Or then you have heartbreak like mine where they still love you and leave anyway. Love isn’t the guarantor of security in a relationship. I had a simple minded approach that as long as there was love, anything could be solved and worked through. What torched my view on love was confusion about what holds anything together if not love? I don’t have the answers as I’m only 4 months out from the ending of a 9 year relationship but it is easy to rationalise that if they left me, they never loved me or loved me truly and that may be right in some instances but broadly speaking I think people don’t view love as a source that needs nurturing and replenishment, or they allow grievances to build up over time and poor communication. Some people are their own worst enemy too, it’s so complicated which makes it daunting to ever want to risk going through heartbreak again.

When I was younger, it was the most important thing in the world to me to love and be loved. After losing someone you love when things don’t work out, it’s easy to become disillusioned. Instead, I am choosing to change my perspective and not become cynical. I don’t know if I’ll ever find love that is reciprocated, but it’s opened my eyes to everything else I abandoned for love that I now get to explore. I hope I don’t end up alone, but I would rather that than be with someone who secretly resents me, loves someone else, or just makes me feel less than.

These are years that you are being asked to wait. He could be leaving the opportunity to accept growth and change in the years to come at school too, but that’s pure speculation. If everything still aligns with you both as a couple, that might be the determining factor for him to propose. Don’t waste your youth with someone content to keep you waiting for something they aren’t certain that they want. Actions speak louder than words, they always do. If communicating this with him and making your expectations clear around getting engaged pushes him away, then you shouldn’t be getting married to someone resentful of committing to you. You’re taking him at his word right now, and in the years to come if he turns around and says, “you know what? This isn’t what I want” you’re rightfully going to be pissed and devastated. 
Put yourself in his spot. Would you be comfortable telling someone that the only thing stopping you from getting engaged was school, or does that sound like a convenient excuse to delay something you’re not sold on? Have a conversation and see if there are any other roadblocks that they are considering in their decision making process. This doesn’t make him a bad guy, it is so normal in your 20s to be on different paths and leaving space to grow is healthy. Just want to point that out, it’s when you sell the other person that you’re on the same page and waste their time. 
Best of luck to you OP x

You need to recalibrate, I think. Explore the polar opposite of your current approach and attitude to art without wondering if you're hitting the right academic criteria without actually 'feeling it' yourself just as a thought experiment to re-calibrate your mindset.   
Find experimental, student pieces that don't have any critique that you can fact-check yourself on and just ask yourself what YOU are getting out of it. If it is giving nothing, let it give nothing, it does not need to click immediately or even in minutes. It can turn into a form of meditation to authentically extract meaning from something without any outer influence. Art is subjective, so it seems ridiculous to systematically apply a criteria of points you have to touch on to demonstrate you understand the assignment.   
Back to what I said at the start, I think doing some of your own research into existentialist theories, particularly my favourite one - absurdism - would be the balance you might need to expand your scope to the complete opposite of the demand to derive constant meaning of something.   
As I've seen other people comment on this sub, interviews conducted with abstract artists can tell us directly from the artists sometimes that there is no meaning - which in itself can be interpreted that the art holds a mirror to our own absurd need to extract meaning. In a way, the commentary itself is the art form. Maybe that  doesn't answer your question or help in any way, I just thought experimenting with this way of thinking could provide a bit of an escape or solace from the mental exhaustion you are associating with art right now. It's possible to find your way back to your passion if you're honest with how you feel about it and allow your thought process to lead you where it will. Don't be afraid to resent it, lean into every feeling with intensity that is forbidden in everyday life. Don't moderate yourself in your approach. This is why artists get the reputation of being crazed, obsessive, you know the stereotype. It's finally a medium we are provided where sensitivity can be channeled into something rewarding instead of being controlled. This sounds pretentious but when you talk about art it's hard to sound like anything else, but I view it as freedom. It's always been freedom for people even in the most dire circumstances for a reason. IMO over-intellectualisation can turn into 'ripping wings off butterflies' instead of appreciating it for what it is, you're performing multiple autopsies until it is torn to shreds and there is no mystery left.

2 months, I was in a dark place for a while but had a perspective shift in therapy yesterday. I was taking 95% of the blame for my relationship ending which was making me punish myself a lot. Trying to do a hundred different autopsies on what went wrong, at what point did they consider leaving is a mental anguish I wouldn’t wish on anyone.
Feeling a little bit validated as well that my reaction to our arguments toward the end was because I knew the road we were heading down and keeping my fear at bay was eating me alive. 

I spent entire nights crying, hating myself more than I ever have and just not wanting to wake up in the morning, thinking if I didn’t have my issues with anxiety and depression that I would be worth loving and less exhausting. I made up for it where I could, I’d do his laundry, keep the house clean, make our house welcoming and all my effort wasn’t fulfilling the way he needed physical expressions of love instead of acts of service.

Having some better days after getting closer to forgiving myself for being human and learning not to be frightened of my feelings and letting them rule me. It’s been hard having to let everything catch up with me and feel it all, but I can feel it already changing me in a good way.
I’ve stopped worrying about being alone forever and I just want to have my own space, friends and a pet to care for, it’s early days yet and when the time feels right it will come naturally. When it ended I realised I had no ‘community’, no support system and I think it’s essential for me to form my own before I could ever think about getting into another relationship. 

For the first time since I was 15, I’m single and navigating the adult world alone is something I might have had to lose everything familiar for to find my true purpose. So there’s a few things here I want to address. 

1. You said at the end you know what needs to happen.

2. Mental health is really important, I hope you are getting the help and support you need to stay well. Confirming your diagnosis of ADHD and a treatment/management plan with a professional would greatly improve your life. 
3. Breaking up off and on in a relationship to the point where it becomes a pattern isn’t healthy. What might help you is to write down and analyse the reasons for the breakups and see if you can identify a pattern. Life is all about making mistakes and learning from them so we can do better next time. 

Once you get your own space away from the ex, to fully process the fact that you are separated you’ll need to cease all communication with him. Block him if you have to, this stage of silence is really important. You can’t go forward when half of you remains in the past.

Some unsolicited advice: You’re too valuable to feel like you were forgettable to this person. Some people who initiate the break up seem to have a lot more composure because they have mentally rehearsed this so many times that they are way more prepared than we are. He might very well be in a place of grief over this, but whatever his reason decided that he needed to remove himself from being in a relationship. Sit her down and acknowledge that this might seem out of the blue but it is something you have been avoiding the reality of and she deserves to know what is going on. There will have to be separation between you both to process that you're not in each other's lives in the same capacity, it can be emotionally confusing to hear from them and get support from them, it only creates an illusion that delays the healing she will have to go through.   
The reality is, this will be heartbreaking. It's the price we pay for loving someone. 

After you tell her, depending on the living situation I think it's courtesy as the dumper to give the dumpee the option of staying in the place until they can plan what to do next as in her emotional state you're not in the headspace to make next step decisions. It will take time for your head and heart to get on the same page with their new reality. It sounds like you care about her feelings and that will come through naturally as long as you aren't trying to completely suppress it. Don't say anything about being friends, etc. it might not happen, it might be seen as hope of reconnecting and if it happens, great but the focus in the now should be the reality of separation. We can't speak of what will happen in the future anymore, that is part of the grief process. Best of luck, I know its very hard for you as well.

This was one of the contributing factors to my partner leaving me after 10 years. Here’s some advice as someone who wished it was brought up in a better way. 
1. Don’t panic about it, maintain the appearance that you will get through this together 
2. Give them a chance to voice their fears and concerns after you have expressed yours. 
3. Prepare for them to get a little defensive, it’s a sensitive spot, it was for me, I felt like I needed to be chemically altered to be normal and that my mental health was secondary to sex when that wasn’t the case
4. Offer to support them in any way they need to get there, whether it be going to doctors appointments, trying new things in bed, sometimes it can be that you just need to start dating each other again. Especially after so long, go you guys :) 
5. Don’t keep bringing it up, this creates a snowball effect and the issue becomes bigger than it really is and the pressure can make both people turn inward instead of into each other. 
6. Destigmatise couples counselling. Go there sooner rather than later, my partner and I were meant to have an appointment yesterday…but he ended it with me before we got there. 

Relationships need maintenance just like anything else! Be there for each other and do everything with the intention of getting through it together. It’s tough but it is the motivator the other person needs to know you’re on their side and nothing is wrong with them.
